state_profile.voting_summary: 2024 was Connecticut's first presidential election with early voting (a 14-day window), and 40% of voters used it; absentee ballots still require an excuse (7% of votes). Polls close at 8 p.m. Eastern; towns report election day and early votes through the evening, with absentees folded in overnight and results essentially complete the same night. Unusually, Connecticut's early in-person vote was its most Democratic mode (D+27 versus D+1 on election day), so the state turns bluer as early votes report.
